source_evidence.observation: The paper defines u as working precision, u_f as factorization precision, and u_r as residual-computation precision, with u_r <= u <= u_f. [PDF p. 1, printed A817, precision bullets and eq. (1.1)]

The effective correction-solve precision satisfies u <= u_s <= u_f. Algorithm 1.1 takes nonsingular A in R^(n x n) and b in R^n, computes the initial solution at u_f, then for i = 0,1,... computes the residual at u_r and rounds it to u_s, solves the correction equation at u_s and stores the correction at u, and performs the update at u. [PDF p. 2, printed A818, u_s definition and Algorithm 1.1]

The analysis uses the standard floating-point model and defines gamma_k = k u/(1-k u); a superscript selects the corresponding unit roundoff, so gamma_p^r = p u_r/(1-p u_r). [PDF p. 5, printed A821, opening of section 2]
The componentwise condition-number convention is cond(A) = norm_inf(abs(A^(-1)) abs(A)); therefore, by substitution, cond(A^(-1)) = norm_inf(abs(A) abs(A^(-1))). [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eq. (2.2)]

The step-4 solver condition is abs(rhat_i - A dhat_i) <= u_s G_i abs(dhat_i). The paper states that G_i is a function of n, A, rhat_i, and u_s and has nonnegative entries. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eq. (2.5) and following sentence]

For componentwise backward-error quotients, a numerator divided by zero is interpreted as zero when the numerator is zero and as infinity otherwise. [PDF p. 6, printed A822, continuation after eq. (2.7)]

The computed residual satisfies rhat_i = b - A xhat_i + Delta r_i and abs(Delta r_i) <= u_s abs(b-A xhat_i) + (1+u_s) gamma_p^r (abs(b)+abs(A)abs(xhat_i)). Here p is the maximum number of nonzeros in a row of [A b], and p = n+1 for dense A and b. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, text preceding and eq. (3.3)]
The rounded update satisfies xhat_(i+1) = xhat_i + dhat_i + Delta x_i with abs(Delta x_i) <= u abs(xhat_(i+1)). [PDF p. 7, printed A823, eq. (3.6)]
The residual identity used by section 5 is A xhat_(i+1) - b = Delta r_i + A dhat_i - rhat_i + A Delta x_i. [PDF p. 9, printed A825, eq. (4.1)]

The derivation defines Z_1 = u_s G_i + (1+u_s) gamma_p^r abs(A) and M_1 = (I-Z_1 abs(A^(-1)))^(-1). If norm_inf(Z_1 abs(A^(-1))) <= 1/2, then I-Z_1 abs(A^(-1)) is an M-matrix, and M_1 exists, is entrywise nonnegative, and has infinity norm at most 2. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, eqs. (5.3)-(5.5) and following paragraph]

Theorem 5.1 assumes Algorithm 1.1, nonsingular A, solver condition (2.5), and u_s norm_inf(G_i abs(A^(-1))) + (1+u_s) gamma_p^r cond(A^(-1)) <= 1/2 for all i. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, Theorem 5.1 and eq. (5.6); quantifier continuation on PDF p. 11, printed A827]

For every i >= 0, the theorem concludes abs(b-A xhat_(i+1)) <= W_i abs(b-A xhat_i) + y_i, where W_i = u_s I + (1+u_s) M_1 Z_1 abs(A^(-1)) and y_i = (1+u_s)(1+u) gamma_p^r (I+M_1 Z_1 abs(A^(-1)))(abs(b)+abs(A)abs(xhat_(i+1))) + u abs(A)abs(xhat_(i+1)). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, continuation of Theorem 5.1]

Only after the theorem does the paper use M_1 = I+O(u_s) and approximate inequalities marked by lesssim to interpret W_i and derive the eventual componentwise relative backward-error estimate (5.8), using Lemma 5.2 and the scaling ratio xi. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, discussion after Theorem 5.1, Lemma 5.2, and eqs. (5.7)-(5.8)]

The unscaled analysis explicitly ignores underflow and overflow; section 6 introduces a different scaled version of steps 4 and 5 to address those events. [PDF p. 12, printed A828, opening of section 6]

binders: Fix a matrix dimension n, a nonsingular matrix A in R^(n x n), and b in R^n; Algorithm 1.1 treats A and b as data stored at working precision u. [PDF p. 2, printed A818, Algorithm 1.1; PDF p. 10, printed A826, Theorem 5.1]
Fix precision parameters u_r, u, u_f, and u_s satisfying u_r <= u <= u_f and u <= u_s <= u_f. [PDF p. 1, printed A817, eq. (1.1); PDF p. 2, printed A818, u_s definition]

The iteration index ranges over i = 0,1,..., with xhat_i, rhat_i, and dhat_i denoting computed iterates, residuals, and corrections in the analysis. [PDF p. 2, printed A818, Algorithm 1.1; PDF p. 7, printed A823, eqs. (3.3) and (3.6)]

For each correction solve, G_i has nonnegative entries and is associated with n, A, rhat_i, and u_s through solver model (2.5). Its n-by-n dimension is forced by the displayed matrix-vector products rather than separately declared. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eq. (2.5) and following sentence]
hypotheses: Explicit theorem hypothesis: Algorithm 1.1 is applied to Ax=b with nonsingular A in R^(n x n). [PDF p. 10, printed A826, opening of Theorem 5.1]
Explicit theorem hypothesis: at every relevant step-4 solve, abs(rhat_i-A dhat_i) <= u_s G_i abs(dhat_i). [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eq. (2.5); PDF p. 10, printed A826, Theorem 5.1]
Explicit uniform hypothesis: u_s norm_inf(G_i abs(A^(-1))) + (1+u_s) gamma_p^r cond(A^(-1)) <= 1/2 for all i. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, eq. (5.6); PDF p. 11, printed A827, words for all i]

Inherited algorithm hypothesis: residuals are formed at u_r and rounded to u_s, corrections are effectively solved at u_s and stored at u, and updates are performed at u. [PDF p. 2, printed A818, Algorithm 1.1]
conclusions: For every i >= 0, abs(b-A xhat_(i+1)) <= W_i abs(b-A xhat_i) + y_i, with the inequality interpreted componentwise. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, continuation of Theorem 5.1; PDF p. 5, printed A821, componentwise-inequality convention]
W_i is exactly u_s I + (1+u_s) M_1 Z_1 abs(A^(-1)). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, continuation of Theorem 5.1]
y_i is exactly (1+u_s)(1+u) gamma_p^r (I+M_1 Z_1 abs(A^(-1)))(abs(b)+abs(A)abs(xhat_(i+1))) + u abs(A)abs(xhat_(i+1)). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, continuation of Theorem 5.1]
definitions_and_conventions: Absolute values of vectors and matrices are entrywise, and inequalities between vectors or matrices are componentwise. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, notation paragraph preceding eq. (2.3)]

cond(B) means norm_inf(abs(B^(-1)) abs(B)); hence cond(A^(-1)) means norm_inf(abs(A) abs(A^(-1))), with this latter expansion inferred by substituting B=A^(-1). [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eq. (2.2); PDF p. 10, printed A826, eq. (5.6)]
gamma_k = k u/(1-k u), and a superscript denotes which unit roundoff replaces u; consequently gamma_p^r = p u_r/(1-p u_r). [PDF p. 5, printed A821, opening of section 2]
p is the maximum number of nonzeros in any row of the augmented matrix [A b]; for dense A and b, p=n+1. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, paragraph preceding eq. (3.3)]
Z_1 is exactly the paper's displayed symbol and is defined by Z_1 = u_s G_i + (1+u_s) gamma_p^r abs(A). [PDF p. 10, printed A826, eq. (5.3)]
M_1 is exactly the paper's displayed symbol and is defined by M_1 = (I-Z_1 abs(A^(-1)))^(-1). [PDF p. 10, printed A826, eq. (5.5)]

The identity I and the matrices Z_1, M_1, and W_i are n-by-n by dimensional conformity, while y_i and each residual magnitude are n-vectors; these dimensions are implicit in the displayed products. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, eqs. (5.3)-(5.5); PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1 continuation]
implicit_context: A and b denote the stored input data, while xhat_i denotes a computed iterate; b-A xhat_i in the theorem is the mathematical residual of that computed iterate, not the separately computed residual rhat_i. [PDF p. 2, printed A818, Algorithm 1.1; PDF p. 7, printed A823, eq. (3.3); PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1 continuation]

The standard floating-point model from section 2 is inherited by Theorem 5.1 even though it is not restated in the theorem. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, opening of section 2; PDF p. 10, printed A826, Theorem 5.1]

Condition (5.6), together with nonnegativity and the definition of cond(A^(-1)), is sufficient for norm_inf(Z_1 abs(A^(-1))) <= 1/2; the preceding M-matrix argument then supplies existence and nonnegativity of M_1 and norm_inf(M_1) <= 2. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eq. (2.2); PDF p. 10, printed A826, eqs. (5.3)-(5.6)]
Theorem 5.1 invokes solver condition (2.5), not solver conditions (2.3) or (2.4). [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eqs. (2.3)-(2.5); PDF p. 10, printed A826, opening of Theorem 5.1]

No special condition on the step-1 solver is added by Theorem 5.1 beyond use of Algorithm 1.1; the theorem's displayed recurrence does not contain u_f. [PDF p. 2, printed A818, Algorithm 1.1 and following paragraph; PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, Theorem 5.1]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The result is tied to the original, unscaled Algorithm 1.1: solve for the initial approximation at u_f and store it at u; for i=0,1,... compute b-A x_i at u_r and round it to u_s, solve A d_i=r_i at u_s and store d_i at u, then update x_(i+1)=x_i+d_i at u. Theorem 5.1 specifically uses the step-4 componentwise defect model (2.5). [PDF p. 2, printed A818, Algorithm 1.1; PDF p. 5, printed A821, eq. (2.5); PDF p. 10, printed A826, Theorem 5.1]
numerical_model: Residual formation has two rounding stages summarized exactly by rhat_i = b-A xhat_i+Delta r_i and abs(Delta r_i) <= u_s abs(b-A xhat_i) + (1+u_s) gamma_p^r (abs(b)+abs(A)abs(xhat_i)). [PDF p. 7, printed A823, eq. (3.3)]

The update model is xhat_(i+1)=xhat_i+dhat_i+Delta x_i with abs(Delta x_i) <= u abs(xhat_(i+1)); the bound uses the rounded output xhat_(i+1), not the unrounded sum. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, eq. (3.6)]
The correction solver is modeled through its computed equation defect: abs(rhat_i-A dhat_i) <= u_s G_i abs(dhat_i). [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eq. (2.5)]
The exact residual b-A xhat_i and computed residual rhat_i are distinct and are connected by Delta r_i. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, eq. (3.3)]

The displayed theorem retains the exact gamma_p^r rational factor and the multiplicative rounding factors 1+u_s and 1+u within the adopted standard model. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, gamma definition; PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1 continuation]
error_notions: Theorem 5.1 bounds the componentwise absolute true residual vector; it is not directly a forward-error statement or a scalar normwise residual bound. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, continuation of Theorem 5.1]

The paper defines componentwise relative backward error omega(y) as the minimum epsilon permitting componentwise relative perturbations to both A and b, equivalently max over components of abs(b-Ay)_j divided by (abs(A)abs(y)+abs(b))_j. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eqs. (2.6)-(2.7)]
The eventual omega bound in equation (5.8) is a subsequent lesssim estimate, not one of Theorem 5.1's exact conclusions. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, eq. (5.8) and preceding text]
The additive vector y_i depends on xhat_(i+1), so the recurrence is not an estimate with an iteration-independent additive constant. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, definition of y_i]
norms: The hypothesis and auxiliary bounds use the infinity norm; the main residual recurrence itself is componentwise and has no enclosing norm. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, eq. (5.6); PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1 continuation]

The condition uses cond(A^(-1)) = norm_inf(abs(A)abs(A^(-1))), not cond(A) = norm_inf(abs(A^(-1))abs(A)); multiplication order is therefore significant. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eq. (2.2); PDF p. 10, printed A826, eq. (5.6)]
The M-matrix argument gives norm_inf(M_1) <= 2 under norm_inf(Z_1 abs(A^(-1))) <= 1/2. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, paragraph following eq. (5.5)]
The later conversion toward omega uses Lemma 5.2: abs(A)abs(x) <= norm_inf(A) xi(x) abs(x), where xi(x)=max_j abs(x_j)/min_j abs(x_j). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, Lemma 5.2]
constants_and_indexing: The recurrence advances exactly from residual index i to residual index i+1 and is asserted for every i >= 0. [PDF p. 2, printed A818, Algorithm 1.1; PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1 continuation]
The uniform threshold in (5.6) is exactly 1/2. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, eq. (5.6)]
W_i has the exact leading term u_s I and multiplier 1+u_s on M_1 Z_1 abs(A^(-1)). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, definition of W_i]
y_i has the exact factor (1+u_s)(1+u) gamma_p^r and the separate final term u abs(A)abs(xhat_(i+1)); neither term may be dropped from the theorem. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, definition of y_i]

The PDF literally uses subscript 1 in Z_1 and M_1, while Z_1's definition contains the iteration-indexed G_i. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, eqs. (5.3) and (5.5); PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1 continuation]
For dense input, the residual accumulation parameter is p=n+1, not n. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, paragraph preceding eq. (3.3)]
higher_order_terms: Theorem 5.1's recurrence, W_i, and y_i are displayed without big-O or lesssim notation; all shown 1+u_s and 1+u factors are retained. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, continuation of Theorem 5.1]
The statement M_1=I+O(u_s) and the lesssim bounds for W_i and norm_inf(W_i) occur only in the interpretation following the theorem. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, discussion and eq. (5.7)]
Equation (5.8) is introduced with Hence, ultimately and uses lesssim, so its omitted terms and constants are not specified by the exact theorem. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, eq. (5.8)]
exceptional_values: Nonsingularity of A is explicit and is required for every occurrence of A^(-1). [PDF p. 10, printed A826, opening of Theorem 5.1]
The unscaled rounding-error analysis ignores underflow and overflow; the scaling modification in section 6 is a different algorithmic variant. [PDF p. 12, printed A828, opening of section 6]
For componentwise backward-error quotients, a zero denominator yields zero when the numerator is zero and infinity otherwise. [PDF p. 6, printed A822, continuation after eq. (2.7)]

The discussion after (5.8) says that a zero component of abs(b)+abs(A)abs(x) makes obtaining a small componentwise relative backward error ill posed. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, paragraph following eq. (5.8)]

undebatable_constraints: The contract must preserve the componentwise residual recurrence abs(b-A xhat_(i+1)) <= W_i abs(b-A xhat_i)+y_i for every i >= 0. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1 continuation]

The solver assumption must be the componentwise defect model (2.5), not the distinct forward-error or normwise models (2.3) and (2.4). [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eqs. (2.3)-(2.5); PDF p. 10, printed A826, Theorem 5.1]

The uniform hypothesis must include both u_s norm_inf(G_i abs(A^(-1))) and (1+u_s) gamma_p^r cond(A^(-1)), with sum at most 1/2 for all i. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, eq. (5.6) and its quantifier]
The order inside cond(A^(-1)) is abs(A)abs(A^(-1)); replacing it by cond(A) changes the source statement. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eq. (2.2); PDF p. 10, printed A826, eq. (5.6)]

W_i, y_i, Z_1, and M_1 must retain their exact displayed factors, matrix order, and the dependence of y_i on xhat_(i+1). [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, eqs. (5.3), (5.5), and Theorem 5.1 continuation]
The residual in the conclusion is the true residual b-A xhat_i, not the computed residual rhat_i. [PDF p. 7, printed A823, eq. (3.3); PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1 continuation]
The exact theorem must not be replaced by the later approximate or ultimate omega estimate (5.8). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, Theorem 5.1 and eq. (5.8)]
The result concerns the unscaled Algorithm 1.1 and inherits the analysis's exclusion of underflow and overflow. [PDF p. 2, printed A818, Algorithm 1.1; PDF p. 12, printed A828, opening of section 6]
The PDF's displayed symbols are Z_1 and M_1, not Z_i and M_i, although Z_1 contains G_i. [PDF p. 10, printed A826, eqs. (5.3) and (5.5)]
Theorem 5.1 does not assume G_i >= abs(A); the paper mentions that relation only as a practical expectation after equation (5.7). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, discussion following eq. (5.7)]

ambiguities.issue: The PDF literally writes Z_1 and M_1, but Z_1 = u_s G_i + (1+u_s) gamma_p^r abs(A) contains the iteration-dependent G_i, and W_i and y_i use Z_1 and M_1. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, eqs. (5.3), (5.5), and Theorem 5.1 continuation]
ambiguities.evidence: No sentence explains whether subscript 1 is intentional fixed notation, a typographical substitute for i, or shorthand for quantities recomputed from each G_i. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, eqs. (5.3), (5.5), and Theorem 5.1 continuation]
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must either preserve the literal Z_1 and M_1 notation while exposing their dependence on G_i, or explicitly record an indexing interpretation; silently changing them to Z_i and M_i would resolve an ambiguity not resolved by the PDF. [PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, cited displays]

ambiguities.issue: The paper defines gamma_p^r = p u_r/(1-p u_r) through the standard model but Theorem 5.1 does not restate a condition such as p u_r < 1. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, gamma definition; PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, Theorem 5.1]
ambiguities.evidence: The theorem imports gamma_p^r and the standard model without an explicit local domain or positivity hypothesis for its denominator. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, opening of section 2; PDF p. 11, printed A827, definition of y_i]
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement must decide whether the usual standard-model side condition is inherited as an assumption or whether gamma_p^r is treated merely as the displayed rational expression; the PDF does not restate that choice in Theorem 5.1. [PDF p. 5, printed A821; PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827]

ambiguities.issue: The later symbols O(u_s) and lesssim are not assigned explicit constants or quantified remainder terms in this passage. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, discussion and eqs. (5.7)-(5.8)]
ambiguities.evidence: They appear only in the interpretation after the exact theorem, including the phrase Hence, ultimately before equation (5.8). [PDF p. 11, printed A827, discussion following Theorem 5.1]
ambiguities.impact: Those later estimates cannot be converted into exact inequalities without adding semantics absent from the passage; they should remain separate from the exact source contract. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, eqs. (5.7)-(5.8)]

ambiguities.issue: Lemma 5.2 defines xi(x)=max_j abs(x_j)/min_j abs(x_j) without restating a zero-denominator convention at the lemma itself. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, Lemma 5.2]
ambiguities.evidence: A prior general quotient convention says division by zero is zero for zero numerator and infinity otherwise, while the later discussion specifically warns about zero components. [PDF p. 6, printed A822, continuation after eq. (2.7); PDF p. 11, printed A827, paragraph after eq. (5.8)]
ambiguities.impact: This affects only the later approximate conversion to omega, not Theorem 5.1's exact residual recurrence; any formalization of Lemma 5.2 or (5.8) must make the convention explicit. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, Lemma 5.2 and eq. (5.8)]

contract_plain_english: Run the original unscaled iterative-refinement algorithm on nonsingular A with the stated four precision parameters. [PDF pp. 1-2, printed A817-A818, eq. (1.1) and Algorithm 1.1] If every computed correction satisfies abs(rhat_i-A dhat_i) <= u_s G_i abs(dhat_i), and if u_s norm_inf(G_i abs(A^(-1))) + (1+u_s) gamma_p^r cond(A^(-1)) <= 1/2 uniformly for all i, then every next computed iterate satisfies the exact componentwise true-residual recurrence abs(b-A xhat_(i+1)) <= W_i abs(b-A xhat_i)+y_i with W_i, y_i, Z_1, and M_1 exactly as displayed above. [PDF p. 5, printed A821, eq. (2.5); PDF pp. 10-11, printed A826-A827, Theorem 5.1] The theorem itself is not equation (5.8): that componentwise relative backward-error estimate is a later, ultimate lesssim interpretation using additional scaling information. [PDF p. 11, printed A827, Lemma 5.2 and eq. (5.8)] Underflow and overflow are excluded from this unscaled analysis. [PDF p. 12, printed A828, opening of section 6]
